summary.intent: Resolve a new review finding on change #54 (NAPI size budget), then have the user get a cohesive, low-ceremony plan that treats all recent findings as one bug class in light of the architecture and semantic models, and finally ask what's next for the release.
summary.outcome: Fixed the section-name budget bug (907839a1) with tests and a sweep, produced a plan to move size accounting into michi-core footprints with a single NAPI acceptance rule, and opened a small PR correcting changeset entries so release PR #131 can be rebuilt with accurate notes. The plan PR stacked on #141 awaits user approval.

repo: Recent review findings on the NAPI layer all stem from three hand-maintained size models disagreeing: per-call Budget (napi/input.rs), HeldBytes/Charge (napi/response.rs), and cost.rs.
AGENTS.md describes napi as a thin shim, but ~1,900 lines (response.rs, cost.rs, hostile test matrix) re-model how michi-core renders, which is architectural drift.
Replacement APIs (AgentResponse.pipeline/partialSuccess with a name arg) must be checked against the removed functions: any payload the old ones accepted should still be accepted.
Existing proptest_toon/proptest_mcp setup and fuzz targets can be extended for a response footprint bound.
0.10 core used `with_hints`, which was needed to correct changeset wording.
Changesets for 0.12 (breaking release) should be consolidated into one JS entry describing limits depending on what renders.

code.finding: Holds the per-call Budget (16 MiB of converted strings); the section name was wrongly counted against it, now checked separately with a 4 KiB cap and counted as structure.
HeldBytes/Charge model with separate 16 and 26 MiB caps; a second model that can diverge from the per-call budget.
Hand-written copy of which names michi-core writers repeat (truncated, totalCount rows); lags behind the writers and is slated for deletion.

workflow: When review findings recur, diagnose the shared structural cause rather than patching each instance.
A Rust test can pass with or without a fix when the stored total never counted the thing; a Node test through the JS per-call check was needed to guard the pipeline case.
Verify with `just check` and `just test` (1,237 Rust, 185 Node tests) at each step.
Check PR state when listings seem incomplete (#140 and #141 were missing from the open list) before assuming something is wrong.

friction: Reviewer kept finding new edge cases after each point fix, since each patch addressed one gap between models.
User asked whether a push was missed; it was actually a new finding, requiring clarification.
Open PR listing showed only #131, requiring extra investigation to find the state of #140 and #141.
Changeset entries named items removed in the release, requiring multiple rewrites and a separate PR.
open_items: Awaiting user decision on building the footprint refactor as a PR stacked on #141 (0.12).
Release PR #131 still waits on the user and must be rebuilt by Callisto after the changeset fix PR merges.
Known documented gap: long section name times many cut cells, since repeats are not limited per call (fixed only by the planned design).

Planned work: core footprints with property tests, switch NAPI to a single acceptance rule, delete cost.rs and Charge/HeldBytes, update spec 04 Input limits, 06-decisions entry, AGENTS.md, and changeset.
Planned fuzz target fuzz/fuzz_targets/response_footprint.rs and mutant testing to validate the output bound.
